newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Local buyers take Sri Lanka stocks to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Local buyers take Sri Lanka stocks to higher close.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks continued to move higher on Monday, propelled by domestic buying of selected stocks, analysts said.
They said investors remained optimistic ahead of Wednesday's budget and good corporate results in the second half of 1996.
The all share index closed up 4.24 points at 615.22. Gainers led losers by 27 to 14, with Hatton National Bank up 13 rupees to 248 and Kotagala Plantations 2.25 to 30.
"Locals, mainly retail investors are taking the index up, expecting the budget to come out with something positive," said Rohan Fernando, a broker at CT Smith.
Turnover was a healthy 43.6 million rupees on local buying of 1.02 million shares of Horana Plantations at 25 rupees, and foreign buying of 85,000 Ceylon Brewery at 30.75.
"Although there are no foreign buy orders on hand, you can find a buyer if you can source quantity," Fernando said.
Many local institutional investors said they were waiting for the budget.

"The index is moving up and company results look good. But we want to see the budget before taking funds from fixed income instruments, which are yielding 18 percent," said the manager of a private pension fund, who declined to be identified.
